title: Cyclic Fatigue Resistance and Fractured Fragment Length of Three Heat-Treated NiTi Rotary Systems: An In Vitro Comparison Including a Novel Instrument
content: Background: This study compared the cyclic fatigue resistance and fractured fragment length of three NiTi rotary systems, including a novel instrument that, according to its manufacturer, is produced using a regional multi-phase heat-treatment protocol. Methods: A total of 60 instruments (n = 20 per group) of One Curve Mini 25/.06, Denco Pro-Flexi 25/.06, and Endo Magic All in One 25/.06 were tested. Cyclic fatigue testing was performed in an artificial canal within a stainless-steel block (60° curvature angle, 5 mm radius of curvature, 1.5 mm internal diameter) in distilled water at 35 ± 1 °C. Instruments were rotated at 300 rpm until fracture. The number of cycles to failure (NCF) was calculated, fragment lengths were measured with a digital caliper, and cross-sectional geometry was evaluated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis and Dunn’s test (α = 0.05). Results: Significant differences were found among the groups for both NCF and fragment length (p < 0.001). The highest NCF was recorded for Endo Magic All in One (9165.50 ± 2049.58), followed by One Curve Mini (3007.50 ± 470.79) and Denco Pro-Flexi (2023.00 ± 1134.43); all pairwise comparisons were significant. Fragments in the Denco Pro-Flexi group were significantly longer (7.51 ± 1.05 mm). SEM revealed circular, triple-helix, and square cross-sections for Endo Magic All in One, One Curve Mini, and Denco Pro-Flexi, respectively. Conclusions: Endo Magic All in One showed significantly higher cyclic fatigue resistance; the underlying metallurgical mechanism could not be confirmed and requires further characterization.
